newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Tough competition rings warning at Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tough competition rings warning at Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish telecoms giant LM Ericsson AB on Tuesday posted a 30 percent jump in nine month profits but rang a warning note that competition at the cutting edge of mobile telephones could hit profit margins.

After U.S. rival Motorala posted weaker third quarter results earlier this month, Ericsson matched market expectations by posting a nine month pre-tax profit of 6.26 billion crowns ($950 million) against 4.81 billion a year ago.
The company said order bookings had risen 22 percent in the nine months to 95.63 billion crowns and net sales by 17 percent to 78.20 billion crowns - largely due to its mobile phone unit.
"Again the very positive development within mobile telecommunications accounted for most of the growth," chief executive Lars Ramqvist said in a statement.
"The mobile telephone business is developing favourably with strong demand for GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) products."
Sales of mobile phones and systems soared 38 percent in the nine months to September 30 as order bookings rose 34 percent.
But the company stressed that it was aware of the competitiveness in the telecoms market and was trying to find ways to prepare itself for a sector battle.

"Ericsson's gross margin weakened slightly (in the nine months) due to increased competition and continuous consideration has been given in the accounts for increased risks related to changes in technology and markets and greater financial exposure," the company said in its report.

Ramqvist said over the past year the company had engaged 500 experts to make in-depth studies of its strategies to boost competitiveness and profitability and boosted the number of staff in its radio telecoms unit by 10,000.
U.S. competitor Motorola partly blamed its weaker third quarter profits on competitive pressures and continuing price declines in cellular telephones.
Aware of the need for new products, Motorola has recently launched "the world's smallest mobile phone", StarTac.
Compared to its mobile phone success, the performance of Ericsson's other divisions were dull.
Its public telecommunications division reported a 19 percent rise in order bookings for comparable units but sales declined to 15.47 billion crowns from 16.35 billion a year ago.

"As a result of strong pressure on prices and delays in China, the business area's sales declined and profitability was weak," the company said. "The process of change, designed to shorten lead times and reduce costs, is continuing."
In the business network unit, net sales rose six percent and order bookings were described as "satisfactory".
The components division reported higher sales and order bookings with strong demand for telecoms cable, energy systems, and microelectronics for mobile telecoms systems.
Order bookings and sales rose in microwave systems. Ericsson said the stronger crown had an effect on pre-tax income, wiping nearly 700 million crowns off the results.

However capital gains from the sale of electrical wholesaler SELGA AB in the second quarter and the divestment of On-Site paging operations in the first quarter provided a 366 million crown boost to pre-tax income.
Ericsson's share price slipped a touch on the result, trading 4.5 crowns lower ahead of the announcement but 5.5 crowns lower at 183.5 crowns at 1220 GMT.
